text: Nouns to verbs: before a spec, milestone or demo, restate the thing as what it does for whom (the 10-15 demo = 'get an investor to believe seekers will use this and Juvo can make money from it, in 10 minutes'). The verb says which fields' methods to bring in (from Felix Rieseberg's 'How to be more ambitious', 10-13; Alex said file it, 10-15).

Every spec or milestone names a judge that runs, not a model's read: a test, e2e gate, invariant check over real data, cost probe or playtest bot. Codex and Grok reviews stay, as second opinions rather than the judge (from Felix Rieseberg's 'How to be more ambitious', 10-13; Alex said file it, 10-15).

Depth goes in at spec time, not as more review rounds: answer the four depth questions when writing the spec (what a top pro would do that we're not asking; the rawest material; their methods and tools; what other than us shows it's right). Review caps stay (from Felix Rieseberg's 'How to be more ambitious', 10-13; Alex said file it, 10-15).

Altitude means building the instruments first: to hand Claude an outcome instead of a task, first give it what it needs to see that outcome itself (logs, real data, devices to reproduce on). Per project, ask what Claude can't see yet. ourPlace chat logs stay behind the HIPAA line (from Felix Rieseberg's 'How to be more ambitious', 10-13; Alex said file it, 10-15).

Reviewer and tester briefs name a field's methods, never a persona to play: a screen-reader accessibility pass (ourPlace), a quant checking lookahead, survivorship and overfitting (wallstbets), investor diligence questions (jobsnearme). Not 'act as X' (from Felix Rieseberg's 'How to be more ambitious', 10-13; Alex said file it, 10-15).

Limits on the ambition frame: 'insist the impossible is reasonable' only with a judge that runs, or the model fakes done; never hand off fun or feel (Alex is that judge); use range as one prompt to pick fields, not a multi-agent crew per task (tokens) (from Felix Rieseberg's 'How to be more ambitious', 10-13; Alex said file it, 10-15).

Alex wants to keep breadth (many projects in parallel) and still finish quality products; the methodology is how. Each project gets a one-line bar like wallstbets' 'beat the index or it's a fun project', used to decide where depth is worth the tokens (10-15).

jobsnearme 10-14 user test (Muse first-time seeker review, Debbie): P0s that every spec's tester had passed: 1,716-min commutes shown as normal, counts that contradict on one screen, ~1 min/$1 values that read as placeholder. The tester checks the spec ('correctness is defined by the spec and the tests'); nobody judged real output across features on real data.

jobsnearme POST-DEMO, drafted 10-15 and NOT in effect: worktree .claude/worktrees/post-demo-methodology (branch post-demo/methodology-draft, unpushed) drafts the spec-template Judge/verb/depth lines, a critic judge check, and a tester split (verifier + new walker), with Codex's and Grok's own role feedback. Alex decides adoption after the demo.

coter-kit PROPOSAL from the 10-15 Codex+Grok role talk (not started; only on Alex's word): relay gives Codex a read-only HEAD export minus the review trail, not an empty folder; canary checked by the relay; impact+confidence severities; a Grok walker mode (scratch-dir Playwright, --always-approve, 30 turns, GET-only and Maps cap in the script). See jobsnearme branch post-demo/methodology-draft.

jobsnearme methodology (Alex 10-15: 1a 2a 3a 4b): AFTER the demo, merge the post-demo/methodology-draft docs first (template judge+walk, critic check 11, verifier, Codex/Grok briefs, walker), then spec the walk harness, then the relay spec (new Codex rubric goes live with it). Grok walks staging, --always-approve in a scratch dir; prod read-only at milestones.

jobsnearme walker Maps budget (Alex 10-15, 4b = 3x one fresh visit): the 10-13 cost probe put one full visit at ~4 billed Google calls, ~$0.024 list ($24/1,000 visits); Routes bills per job open plus a minimap load. Cap per walk: 3 computeRoutes, 12 billed Google requests (~$0.07), enforced in the Playwright script; a capped commute is expected, not a finding.

coter-kit (Alex 10-15, 5a): AFTER the demo, change the outside-review relay so every project gets it: Codex in a read-only HEAD export minus the review trail, canary checked by the relay, impact+confidence severities, and a Grok walker mode (scratch-dir Playwright, --always-approve, 30 turns, GET-only and Maps cap in the script).

Most process gains come from asking the right questions, including asking the agent that does the work once it has the goals: before a role brief becomes standing, ask the agent filling it how it should be written, then show each model the other's answer for one cross-exam round. Verify factual admissions (Grok: no browser tool, checked) (Alex, 10-15).
